static_traits.name: Li Dylan
static_traits.marital_status: Proposed to girlfriend of three years (unmarried)
static_traits.social_status: Has a girlfriend to confide in, but not yet discussing self-criticism and inadequacy with her
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy or mental-health history; no similar problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to self-Reflect; strong self-criticism, often using 'should/must' sentence patterns; fairly cooperative

basic_info.main_problem: Believing watching <South Park> daily makes one a 'failure', triggering inadequacy and self-criticism; as daily watching and self-criticism continue, the problem keeps escalating, appearing daily while watching TV, also affected by three jobs' Work pressure and the not-yet-realized ideal career.
basic_info.core_demands: After realizing self-criticism affects self-esteem and mental health, hoping to reduce these Self-denial thoughts through counseling.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether I am continuously efficient and productive
Relaxing / watching TV equals laziness and failure

special_situations.event: Sits down to watch 'South Park' as a daily relaxation time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I watch TV or rest, it means I am lazy and a failure; only continuous high efficiency has value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing themselves to reduce television time, using work to divert attention, making strict schedules in order to stay efficient
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a failure; I should improve myself instead of wasting time

special_situations.event: Juggling three jobs but not yet entering the ideal career (baseball announcer)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep working hard and quickly enter the ideal career, it proves I am useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Works overtime, sacrifices rest, uses self-criticism to push oneself forward
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not keep working hard, I will never reach my goals and stay stuck in meaningless Work forever

special_situations.event: When trying to make plans for work and relaxation or practicing self-compassion
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am gentle with myself or allow rest, I will become lazier and lower my standards
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Refuses self-compassion, maintains self-control through harshness, continues to avoid relaxation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Self-compassion will only make me lazier

special_situations.event: Notices work performance is better after rest but still feels guilty and ignores positive information
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive effects do not count; only nonstop Work has value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Denying the benefits of rest, continuing to criticize self and reducing relaxation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The benefits of rest are not important; I am still lazy

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and prove self-worth, able to move toward the ideal career and rest peacefully without being blamed
core_conflict.fear: Fears that once relaxed, one will fail, be seen as lazy, and disappoint significant others
defense_goal: Avoids failure and disappointment by maintaining intense self-criticism and productivity
Constrains oneself with harsh inner rules to gain a sense of security

object_relations.self_representation: A lazy/failed self (someone needing constant self-whipping)
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges / others with high expectations (including social standards and significant others)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes the suggestion of 'allowing rest / practicing self-compassion'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands the counselor's support as indulging one's laziness, which will lower standards and lead to failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, rational tone emphasizes the reason of 'worrying I will become lazier', raises many concerns, avoiding emotional expression and concrete attempts

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing whether one should relax and guilt appears
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes only sustained high efficiency is safe; regards rest as a mistake
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using 'should/must' sentence patterns, emphasizing social standards, serious tone, refusing to explore gray areas

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When probed about shame/worthlessness emotional experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Explains problems with abstract efficiency principles, avoids directly touching emotions
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds with rational analysis and goal-management terminology, reduces emotional vocabulary and subjective feeling descriptions

manifestations: Juggling three jobs at once yet feeling these jobs are 'meaningless'
Views relaxation as a waste of time, hard to gain a sense of meaning from leisure
Bound by introjected rules (must stay efficient), hard to freely choose rest
Equating rest with failure, unable to grant self permission

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes external high-efficiency standards as the sole basis of one's own worth
Equating rest with failure and thus engaging in Self-denial

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Refuses to try self-compassion for fear of becoming lazy
In planning and execution, is highly vigilant about mistakes and finds it hard to relax

positive_force: Has responsibility and drive (handles three jobs at once)
Proactively seeks counseling; willing to try small steps and make plans
Notices that rest helps improve work performance
Having partner support resources (though not yet used)
negative_force: Introjecting productivity as a value condition, strong 'should/must' self-Demands
Excessive self-criticism and shame, tends toward emotional reasoning
Future-predicting worries: fearing never achieving goals without sustained effort
Negating positive evidence and the value of rest
High workload leads to a cycle of exhaustion and guilt

target_behavior.behavior: When watching television, experiences strong self-deprecation and guilt (emotional self-criticism)
antecedent: Sits down to watch 'South Park' or enters leisure time
Thinking of the not-yet-realized ideal career
Seeing cues related to efficiency or goals
target_behavior.core_reason: The introjected belief equating productivity with self-worth, making rest/TV-watching interpreted as laziness and failure.
target_behavior.function: Driving oneself to stop resting and return to Work through self-criticism, to escape failure feelings and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, Emotional exhaustion, declining leisure experience, further affecting Work satisfaction and the relationship with the girlfriend

antecedent: When planning rest or being advised to practice self-compassion
Feeling guilty or worrying about becoming lazy
target_behavior.core_reason: Future-predicting worries and 'should'-rule driven, worrying relaxation will lead to failure and disappoint others
target_behavior.function: Escapes guilt and the risk of being seen as lazy, maintaining a surface sense of control and safety
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening fatigue, fluctuating performance, Reduced enjoyment of life, the problem cycle Reinforced
